title: Cash Flow Template Reading
instructions: Read workbook tables as accounting templates, not generic spreadsheets.
Prefer month headers across columns when a row contains Jan-Dec, M1-M12, or similar period labels.
Do not treat formula results or ordinary amounts as period labels.
Treat Total, YTD, and annual summary columns as summaries, not writable period targets.
For direct cash flow templates, editable line items are usually leaf rows under operating, investing, and financing sections.
For direct cash flow templates, direction must reflect row meaning and numeric signs; payroll, rent, marketing, admin, taxes paid, capex, interest paid, and dividends paid are outflows.
For direct cash flow templates, debt drawdown, equity injection, customer receipts, refunds/other inflows, and asset sale proceeds are inflows when row evidence supports it.
For indirect cash flow templates, formula rows can be valid summary row bindings, but formula-only input rows need human review.
Opening cash labels include opening balance, opening cash, cash at beginning, and beginning cash.
Closing cash labels include closing balance, closing cash, cash at end, and ending cash.
Return only the requested structured decision; deterministic code will build the full template config.
